CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right index finger pain from skiing injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ms. James is a 42-year-old female who presents with right index finger pain sustained during a skiing accident last Saturday, approximately 5 days ago. She was skiing double black diamond slopes when she lost control, fell, and jammed her right index finger on an object. She denies other injuries from the fall. Pain is rated 7/10. She has tried ibuprofen without significant relief. She has not used ice or a splint prior to this visit.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies injuries other than to right index finger.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic constipation.
Appendectomy at age 7.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for chronic constipation.
Ibuprofen (over-the-counter, taken for current injury).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recreational skier.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right hand x-ray: Normal, no fractures, all bones and joints in appropriate alignment.
Palpation: Tenderness to direct pressure on right index finger, pain with longitudinal traction, and pain with compression over the distal interphalangeal joint and proximal interphalangeal joint.

RESULTS
Right hand x-ray: No fractures; normal anatomy.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right index finger distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint sprain.
Plan: Apply splint to right index finger. Start Mobic 15 mg once daily for 14 days as anti-inflammatory. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess healing and determine if hand therapy is needed.
